notes: Tatoeba #143825 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 水が飲みたい。 “I want to drink some water.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Only spelling: 水.

Tatoeba #125498 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 庭の花は美しい。 “The flowers in the garden are beautiful.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 花; 鼻 (nose) is ruled out by にわの and the gloss; 華 is a literary variant and is not accepted.
Tatoeba #189727 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 雨が降るそうだ。 “They say it will rain.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 雨; 飴 (candy) is ruled out by ふる and the gloss.

after: を さんびき つった。
notes: Tatoeba #108413 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 彼は魚を３匹釣った。 “He caught three fish.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 魚; 肴 is a different word; つった fixes the meaning.
Tatoeba #150316 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 次の駅で降ります。 “I am getting off at the next station.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 駅; 液 and 益 are ruled out by つぎの〜で おります and the gloss.

before: かれは がっこうを よく
gloss: to be absent, to take time off
notes: Tatoeba #108870 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 彼は学校をよく休む。 “He often absents himself from school.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 休む, okurigana む shown. No competing everyday spelling.
Tatoeba #229710 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 高い建物ですね。 “That is a high building, is it not?” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 高い, okurigana い shown; たてもの makes the height sense clear.
Tatoeba #231367 (CC BY 2.0 FR): あの犬は大きい。 “That dog is big.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 大きい as a predicate, okurigana きい shown, so 大きな is not the target.
Tatoeba #78845 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 羊は草を食べる。 “Sheep feed on grass.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 食べる, okurigana べる shown. No competing everyday spelling.

before: かれは しんしゃを
notes: Tatoeba #103766 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 彼は新車を買った。 “He bought a new car.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 買った (買う), okurigana った shown; 勝った and 飼った are ruled out by しんしゃを and the gloss.
Tatoeba #4849 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 待つしかない。 “I can only wait.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 待つ, okurigana つ shown; 松 is ruled out by しかない and the gloss.
Tatoeba #155294 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 私は速く泳げる。 “I can swim fast.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 泳げる (泳ぐ), okurigana げる shown. No competing everyday spelling.

after: に いく じかんよ。
notes: Tatoeba #184467 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 学校に行く時間よ。 “It's time to go to school.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 学校. No everyday homophone.
Tatoeba #105758 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 彼は私の先生です。 “He is my teacher.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 先生; 先制, 宣誓 and 専制 are ruled out by わたしの and the gloss.

after: に かさを わすれた。
notes: Tatoeba #124806 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 電車に傘を忘れた。 “I left my umbrella on the train.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 電車; 列車 is a different word.
Tatoeba #229331 (CC BY 2.0 FR): いい天気ですね。 “It is a nice day, isn't it?” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 天気; 転機 is ruled out by いい〜ですね and the gloss.

after: を さんぽしましょう。
notes: Tatoeba #174014 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 公園を散歩しましょう。 “Let's take a walk in the park.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 公園; 講演, 公演 and 後援 are ruled out by さんぽ and the gloss.
Tatoeba #179875 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 近くに病院がある。 “There is a hospital nearby.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 病院; 美容院 is read びよういん, a different word.
Tatoeba #155984 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 私は宿題を終えた。 “I've finished my homework.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 宿題. No everyday homophone.
Tatoeba #104466 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 彼は手紙を書いた。 “He wrote a letter.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 手紙. No everyday homophone.
Tatoeba #194438 (CC BY 2.0 FR): もうすぐ夏休みです。 “Soon there will be summer vacation.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 夏休み, okurigana み shown.

after: に ほんを かえした。
notes: Tatoeba #143874 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 図書館に本を返した。 “She took the book back to the library.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 図書館; 図書室 is a different word.
Tatoeba #154827 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 私は動物園へ行った。 “I went to the zoo.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 動物園. No everyday homophone.
Tatoeba #105211 (CC BY 2.0 FR): 彼は自転車で通学する。 “He goes to school by bicycle.” Kana from the Tatoeba furigana transcription. Answer 自転車. No everyday homophone.
